newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 10.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 10.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Thursday and main factors likely to affect trading.
* After Wednesday's holiday, the Philippine stock market is expected to continue its free-fall today.

The composite index "seems to be in the mood these days to challenge all support levels in its way and the next easy target is 2,880," Sun Hung Kai Securities (Phils) Inc said in an advisory to clients.
Sun Hung Kai pegged the next market support at the 2,800 level if the market breaks 2,880.

* Fears of a crash in Philippine property prices due to a glut and its effect on the banking industry, along with prospects of a further rise in U.S. interest rates, will continue to weigh down stock prices, said Kenneth Nerecina, research head at Vicker Ballast Securities.
The Victorias Milling Corp financial crisis and rumours of board unrest in San Miguel Corp is also affecting market sentiment, he said.
The Busang gold controversy also spilled over to the local mining industry.

"It seemed like we are repeating our experience in 1994 when share prices tumbled after hitting a record high early that year due to a confluence of both domestic and international concerns that include concerns on the effect of the oil, transport and power increases, the Mexican economic crisis and the series of U.S. rate hikes," he said.
* The Philippine Stock Exchange composite index closed on Tuesday at 2,909.30 points, down 81.66. The stock exchange was close on Wednesday due to a holiday.
* The Dow Jones dropped 45.32 points to 6,563.84 points on Wednesday.
* The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) has elected businessman Jose Luis Yulo Jr as its new president, the exchange said on Tuesday.
Yulo is currently president of the government's Philippine International Trading Corp (PITC) and a founding member and former president of the Philippine Chamber of Commerce and Industry.

* The Philippine government has no plans to unseat Andres Soriano III as chairman and chief executive officer of food and beverage firm San Miguel Corp (SMC), the Presidential Commission on Good Government (PCGG) said on Tuesday.
PCGG, state custodian of sequestered shares of companies allegedly owned by late president Ferdinand Marcos and his business associates, holds 48 percent of San Miguel.
* Southeast Cement Holdings Inc said on Tuesday its board approved an expansion programme of 2.5 million tonnes per year for its unit Lloyds Richfield Industrial Corp.
The expansion project is estimated to cost ten billion pesos and is expected to be completed in 27 months, the company said.
